one_liner: Ramp has a broad REST Developer API with OAuth2 (client credentials and authorization code), a sandbox, webhooks, an OpenAPI schema and a vendor-run MCP server. Publishing an app to other Ramp businesses needs Ramp's partner and production-access approvals.
auth_notes: Grant types are Client Credentials, Authorization Code and Refresh Token. The token endpoint is usually called with HTTP Basic client_id:client_secret, but that is only the OAuth2 token exchange.
access_notes: An admin of a Ramp account can create a developer app and get credentials for their own business. Without a Ramp account, a sandbox can be requested through a form. Publishing to other Ramp businesses takes two approvals (partner application, then production access). Some scopes are partner-only or need a support ticket, and some endpoints need a plan feature.
blocker_notes: Multi-user OAuth for other Ramp businesses requires a partner application and a production access application, both reviewed by Ramp. Own-business use needs a Ramp account with admin access. The exact MCP URL is not stated on the fetched pages; it comes from the draft and the Composio signal.

evidence.quote: | **Authorization Code** | Third-party apps, public integrations | Authorized user consent required |
To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.

Publishing an app for other Ramp businesses takes two approvals: a partner application, which gives you access to a Developer console, and a production access application for your app, which you submit from the Developer console.
Don't have a Ramp account? Request a sandbox to start building right away.
Canonical OpenAPI schema for the Developer API: [/openapi/developer-api.json](https://docs.ramp.com/openapi/developer-api.json).
For Ramp's own MCP server and CLI, see [Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI](<#ramp-mcp-and-ramp-cli>).
Connect agents to Ramp via MCP or the CLI. Read data, process approvals, make purchases.
